devil_text.final_recommendation:
The label survives: XR_neumom h=20 continuous residual rank, long top-20, with the bottom-30% avoid list. It reproduces exactly from independent code, carries no leakage, generalises across entity halves (even with half-trained models), is not a simple factor tilt (factor-adjusted DEV alpha +17.7%, t 4.5), and is smooth across K, step, cost and lag. The judges' stack, with no regime layer and no event sleeve, should stand. It survives only with these caveats:

1. Planning numbers. Plan on about +5%/yr excess over the equal-weight universe or random (range 0-10%), not DEV's +16%. 2026 shows intact IC but no measurable long-book profit: seed ensemble -0.2%/yr. Multiple testing at N about 2,000 leaves DSR 0.63-0.76, and the Bonferroni-haircut excess is +6.7%.
2. Execution. Ship a 3+ seed rank ensemble and stagger entries daily or weekly; never report a single seed and phase. Trade at the next open with no delay: each day of delay costs about 1.9 pp/yr.
3. Capacity. Hard limit of about Rs 25 lakh per name (about Rs 20 cr AUM), with a participation cap of 5% of 20-day median ADV. Switch to liq5 above that. Rs 1 Cr per name is not viable: DEV CAGR falls to 6-18% depending on the impact coefficient Y.
4. Avoid veto. Treat the avoid veto (+3.4% DEV, +0.9 to +1.7% in 2026 across all perturbations) as the most reliable component.
5. Kill rule. Pre-register a paper or small-size live period of at least 6 months (about 25 weekly cohorts) before scaling. Kill or review if rolling 6-month excess vs random falls below -5%, or if the IC drops below 0.02.
6. Unknown remaining edge. Disclose that the book is short momentum and long liquidity by construction, so momentum-led small-cap rallies like 2026 will look bad on a relative basis.

html_tables.title: 1. Does the stock-picking book beat simple alternatives? (frozen PROD vs single model vs 3-seed ensemble)
html_tables.note: Phase-averaged (weekly book started on each of the 5 weekdays, averaged). Excess = annualised mean daily difference; t-stats are Newey-West (lag 20). 2026 is a holdout never used for selection. The Nifty 500 is a price index (dividends ~1.2%/yr missing) while lab stock prices include dividends, so the random/equal-weight books are the fair yardsticks. PROD stays the production score regardless (pre-registered).

html_tables.title: 2. Calendar-year returns of the frozen PROD book (one continuous book, 50 bps)
html_tables.note: 2023 starts in the first week of January; 2026 runs to mid-October (holdout). Differences are compounded returns minus compounded returns. The separate fresh-start 2026 holdout book (table 1) starts its four sleeves one week apart in January, so its absolute 2026 return differs from this continuous book; the excess vs random is near zero in both.

html_tables.title: 2b. Quarter-by-quarter returns of the frozen PROD book (one continuous book, 50 bps)
html_tables.note: Quarters in 2026 are holdout. Compounded quarterly returns; differences are return minus return.

ADOPTED (passes the rule; gain is mostly the overnight premium, see table 4)

Random picks gain almost as much from the same timing, so the model's skill (excess vs a random book with the same timing) is essentially unchanged.

Names the PROD book sells at a rebalance

The overnight move is broad (not a few outliers) and present in the more liquid names too, but it shrank from 2023-24 to 2026. Selling at the open captures it; selling at the close (the frozen book) forgoes it.

html_tables.title: 5. Capacity: returns after market impact by fund size (frozen book)
html_tables.note: Each name gets AUM/80. Impact per side = Y x daily vol x sqrt(position / 20-day median traded value), capped at 10%, plus 50 bps base cost. Capped policies hold at most 5% of a name's ADV and leave the rest in cash. Idle cash earns the Nifty 1D Rate. References: equal-weight universe CAGR 0.1122 (2023-25) / 0.0860 (2026); Nifty 500 price 0.1659 / -0.1093.

columns: Share of picks above 10% of ADV
Average fill under a 5% ADV cap
html_tables.note: Frozen book: about 39 orders per week (buys + sells), about 74 names held on a typical day (80 slots), 986 round trips per year; executable carry (X3) cuts orders to about 36 per week.

html_tables.title: 8. Tax illustration for an Indian individual (Jan 2023 - Oct 2026)
rows: Long-term gain 12.5% above Rs 1.25 lakh, paid at sale
Long-term gain 12.5% above Rs 1.25 lakh, paid at sale
html_tables.note: Simplified calendar-year model: tax paid each year-end from the book; short-term losses carried forward; STT (0.1% buy + 0.1% sell) is not deductible from capital gains, so taxable gain = net P&L + STT. Frequent trading may be assessed as business income instead (slab rate; STT then deductible). Nifty 500 is a price index (dividends excluded, which would add ~1.2%/yr before dividend tax). A label whose up share swings from ~13% to ~83% of stocks and moves 0.7-0.9 with the market is mostly describing the market, not the stock. The relative labels hold exactly 30% up every day by construction. Absolute labels' 'up' P&L is high by construction (the class is defined by the outcome); what matters is what can be predicted in advance (table 7).

html_tables.note: Equal-weight averages, re-balanced daily, before costs: not a tradable strategy (a daily round trip costs ~0.5%, more than the ~0.2-0.3% average gap). The pattern holds in every liquidity third, so it is not only an illiquid-stock artefact; part of it may be how NSE's open (auction / first trade) and close (last-30-minute average) prints are formed. Its practical meaning: a signal computed at the close can only be bought at the next open, after the gap has already been paid.

html_tables.title: 7. The final investment process (what the trader does each week)
rows: XR_neumom, 20 days: each day, rank stocks by their next-open-to-20-day-close return after removing what beta, volatility, size (turnover) and 12-1 momentum explain. Top 30% = +1, bottom 30% = -1 (for reporting).
PROD: average rank of 10 LightGBM models (5 seeds x 2 date halves), 55 point-in-time features, retrained once a year on all data up to 22 trading days before 1 January.
NSE EQ-series equities with price >= Rs 20, 20-day turnover >= Rs 2 cr, >= 120 trading days of history, not circuit-locked, ATR 0.5-15%.

One fixed weekday: after the close, rank the universe. Capital is split into 4 sleeves (25% each); each week one sleeve is renewed. A sleeve holds the top 20 names, 1/20 of the sleeve each (about 80 slots, about 74 names held). Hold 20 trading days.

At a sleeve's renewal, keep names that are still in its new top 20; sell the rest and buy the new names in the next morning's opening session (pre-open auction). No stops, no early exits, no volatility-based sizing (all rejected).
Bottom 30% of PROD on the signal day is a do-not-buy list for anything outside the model book (own ideas, tips). Never short it in cash; F&O shorts lost money and are not used.

Fully invested. Holding 80% or 60% (rest in an overnight fund) is allowed purely as a risk-appetite dial; no market-timing governor; a Nifty futures hedge is optional and costs about 8-9%/yr in a rising market.
At most about Rs 20 cr; each order <= 5% of the stock's 20-day median traded value (excess stays in cash).
Budget 0.5% round trip (0.223% statutory + up to 0.14% slippage per side vs the official open); stress test 0.8%.
Weekly dashboard; review if any of: 6-month lead < -5%, 3-month IC < 0.02, 12-month lead < 0. Stop new entries only if the 12-month lead < 0 AND the 3-month IC < 0.02 at the same weekly check.
html_tables.note: Everything except the X3 execution timing was frozen before round 3. X3 is a disclosed post-hoc execution convention; skill is always judged against random picks traded with the same timing.
